seo.title: Heat Transfer Calculator - Conduction Convection
seo.description: Heat Transfer Calculator — Calculate heat transfer rate Q through a wall or surface using the conductive/convective heat transfer equation with instant results & multiple unit support.

formula.explanation: Q = U × A × ΔT. Heat transfer rate equals overall heat transfer coefficient × area × temperature difference. U in W/(m²·K), A in m², ΔT in K.

inputs.label: Heat Transfer Coefficient (U)
inputs.hint: Air free convection: 5-25; forced air: 25-250; liquid: 100-1000

content.introduction: The fundamental heat transfer equation Q = U·A·ΔT calculates heat flow across a surface or through a composite wall. U (overall heat transfer coefficient) combines convection on both sides and conduction through the material.

example.description: A 10 m² wall with U=25 W/m²K across 20°C ΔT loses 5,000 W (5 kW).

faq.a: Insulated building wall: 0.2-0.5 W/m²K; uninsulated brick wall: 2-3; window single pane: ~5; forced-air heat exchanger: 25-100; shell-and-tube liquid-liquid: 300-1000.

faq.q: How do I calculate U from k (conductivity)?
faq.a: For a flat wall: U = k/L (conductivity/thickness). For composite walls: U = 1/Σ(L_i/k_i) including convection resistances on each side.
